title: Tiling prober + shared-workspace reclamation to reduce v3 fragmentation regressions
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: After enabling FlashAttention v3 on multi-tenant nodes we observe intermittent latency spikes and OOMs for medium-length contexts (1k-2k tokens). Root cause analysis shows workspace fragmentation: v3 allocates per-tiling buffers with variable sizes, leaving many small free ranges that prevent later large allocations and force fallback to slower kernels or eviction. This ticket implements a non-invasive runtime-level prober and reclamation layer that 1) probes shape/tiling distribution at runtime (tiling prober), 2) opportunistically coalesces and reclaims free workspace ranges between requests (shared-workspace reclaimer), and 3) exposes a conservative fallback throttle and rollout gating to avoid regressions during canaries.

Scope and goals:
- Add lightweight tiling-prober component that maintains percentiles of tile-size histograms per model family and tenant.
- Implement reclamation pass that runs during quiet cycles (end of decode or small gaps) to defragment workspace without stalling hot decode paths.
- Wire a SLO-aware decision function: if reclamation would add >X ms to critical path, schedule background reclamation instead.
- Provide telemetry dashboards (tile heatmap, fragmentation ratio, reclamation time, effective fallback rate) and tie alerts to >5% regression vs baseline.
- Validate across v2/v3 combinations and on quantized (4/8-bit) builds.

Trade-offs considered:
- Eager defragmentation vs. background reclamation: eager lowers short-term fallbacks but risks latency spikes; we bias toward background when p95 latency is near SLO.
- Per-tenant aggressive coalescing may starve other tenants; reclamation is tenant-scoped with quota and admission controls.
- Complexity: prefer a conservative algorithm first (best-fit merge of adjacent free frames, max coalesce time 2ms) and iterate if necessary.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting allocator or changing GPU drivers. Keep changes in runtime memory manager layer.
acceptance_criteria: Tile-prober producing per-model-family histograms and percentile metrics in telemetry
Reclamation pass reduces fragmentation ratio by >=40% on synthetic fragmentation workload
No p99 regression >5% when enabled under canary traffic compared to baseline v3 without reclamation
Automated test harness covering: fragmented coldstart, steady-state mixed sizes, tenant-quotas enforcement
PR merged with unit+integration tests and a rollout plan in Console (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full)
tasks: Design tiling prober protobuf and in-memory histogram shard layout
Implement reclamation algorithm with configurable time budget and tenant quotas
Add SLO-aware gating and canary rollout flags (runtime config)
Integrate telemetry: tile heatmap, fragmentation ratio, reclaim-op latency
Create synthetic bench workload and run v2/v3 comparators across G4/G5 instances
Write unit tests for allocator coalescing and integration tests for end-to-end refilling/fallback scenarios
Author runbook for detected regressions and automatic rollback thresholds
